title: Government plans cancer centres in every division and a national lab
excerpt: No budget or date yet. Bangladesh still has no national cancer registry, and most care is in Dhaka and Chattogram.

image.alt: The National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital in Mohakhali, Dhaka

content:
The government has begun work on a national molecular biology laboratory for cancer research and plans cancer treatment services in every divisional city, State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr M A Muhit said in Dhaka on Friday, 13 November. He spoke at the opening of the sixth Bangladesh Breast Cancer Conference, reported by Prothom Alo (in Bangla) and The Business Standard.

What the minister said

  • A national molecular biology laboratory, on which work has started. No cost, site or completion date was given.
  • Regional cancer centres in divisional cities, linked to nearby district hospitals for first care and referral, according to Prothom Alo.
  • A new cancer institute, modern equipment for cancer institutes, and training for specialists at home and abroad.
  • A digital e-health system that would allow a national cancer registry. Prothom Alo reports that Bangladesh has no national cancer registry yet.
  • Affordable screening for women in certain age groups to find breast cancer early. The age range was not given.

"The later cancer is detected, the greater the complications and the risk of it spreading to other parts of the body," Dr Muhit said, according to The Business Standard.

Late diagnosis

Citing a study, the minister said more than half of breast cancer patients reached hospital late: 22% at stage two to three and 31% at stage four, and 34% saw the disease return or spread. Prothom Alo did not name the study or its sample. Specialised cancer care is now available mainly in Dhaka and Chattogram, while about 80% of people live in villages, he said.

The conference was organised by the Bangladesh Society for Breast Cancer Study and chaired by its president, Prof Kamruzzaman Chowdhury.

The gap NGOs fill

Families from outside Dhaka often rent rooms near hospitals for months. Prothom Alo English reported on Friday that the Bangladesh Cancer Aid Trust (BANCAT) runs Mosabbir Memorial Alok Nibash in Bashundhara, which gives free rooms, meals, nursing checks, counselling and ambulance transport to 85 patients and carers. The trust says it has supported more than 2,500 people since 2019, funded by individual and corporate donations.

Why it matters

No budget or timeline was announced, so these are plans rather than funded projects. A cancer registry and divisional centres would change where patients travel and what support NGOs need to give. Health NGOs running screening, palliative care or patient support should watch for these plans in the health sector programme and the next budget.

What to watch

Whether the Health Ministry publishes a costed plan, and whether a project for the laboratory or regional centres goes to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).
